title: Purva-vibhaga. Lahari 1. Obeisances to the Vaishnavas
html:
Mangala-shlokas to Shyamananda, Rasikananda and the Gosvamis; a song of obeisance to the guru Shyamananda and his wives, to Sri Chaitanya, Nityananda, Advaita and their associates, to the holy places, to Shyamananda's disciples and Rasikananda's companions; the author's humility and the fruit of hearing the Rasika-mangala

Glory to Sri Sri Radha and Govinda!
Sri Sri Rasika-mangala.
Purva-vibhaga.
The first lahari.
Glory to Sri Sri Rasikananda-deva!

S1. How many, how many Puranas and Itihasas are there not in the world! Yet in them
nowhere did Krishna Himself write anything, except in the Gita-govinda.
Likewise among devotees nowhere is a mark in the form of a dot inscribed by one's own hand —
only for Sri Shyamananda did Srimati Radhika Herself joyfully make [it].1,2,3

S2. A treasury of deep bliss, an ocean of grace, a treasury of the beauty of the three worlds, a treasury and abode of the nectar of the rasa of full prema, a treasury of the Lakshmi of good fortune, the one great treasury of the afflicted, a treasury of tenderness,4 a treasury of the pastimes of compassion — all glory to Shyamananda, the treasury of mercy, whose mind is filled with sweetness!

S3. Bestower of deep bliss, exalter of rasa, a mine of the bhava of Sri Krishna,
giver of peace to the heart, destroyer of darkness, bringer of good to the host of devotees,
cutter of sorrow, prolonger of happiness, maker of the wealth of compassion,
deliverer of the lowly — to Prabhu Rasikananda, [like] the sun, I bow.

S4. O Sri Sanatana Prabhu, ocean of compassion!
O Rupa, whose merciful glance is the only [refuge] of the wretched!
O pair of Bhattas! O wise Raghunatha Dasa!
O Sri Jiva! Quickly show mercy to me, whose mind is dull.5

S5. I worship the two lotus feet of Sri Shyamananda-deva,
by meditating on which people attain prema-bhakti for Hari.

S6. I worship the two feet of Rasikendra — the highest good,
the support of the essence of all sweetness, the highest festival.6

S7. His face is the moon, his speech nectar, Bharati is in his throat;
his beauty is Lakshmi, his sweet smile is lovely — a row of kunda flowers;
his teeth are pearls, his pair of eyes a pair of bees, his arms two lotus stalks:
may people serve this Sri Murari like a chintamani gem.7

Raga Karuna-shri.8
Ghosha: "Rama, glory [to You]! Govinda, Rama, glory [to You]!"

1Song. I worship the feet of Sri Guru — Shyamananda-raya,
by whose mercy attachment to Krishna arose.

2By his mercy comes release from the bonds of worldly existence;
by his mercy all people became full of bhakti.

3Such is Shyamananda: by the touch of his feet
the people of the three worlds float in the rasa of prema-bhakti.

4To poor, lowly, miserable people he showed great mercy;
out of compassion he won over the three worlds.

5The moon of the cowherd clan, shining forth in Utkala,9
he destroyed the darkness of sin by giving prema-bhakti.

6Prabhu is an ocean of bliss, a sea of mercy;
surpassing the three worlds, the beauty of his body is charming.

7Prabhu is a sea of prema, an ocean of nectar;
fortunate in every way, a treasury of tens of millions and hundreds of thousands.

8He dispels the torment of the three worlds;
at his compassionate words everyone's heart melts.

9The crest-jewel of all sweetness is Shyamananda;
age after age he performs pastimes, having descended [into the world].10

10Be merciful to me, Prabhu, son of Durika:11
I shall describe the glory of your dear devotee.

11Then I worship the wives of the guru — the three Thakuranis,12
by whose mercy I know prema-bhakti for Krishna.

12Prema for Krishna embodied, bhakti itself —
she is praised in the world as a disciple of Hridayananda.13

13Show your favour, wife of Shyamananda,
so that with my mouth I may proclaim the glory of Rasika.

14I worship Sri Krishna Chaitanya, Svayam Bhagavan,
who gave prema-bhakti to all living beings.

15Descending age after age, the son of Shachi,
destroying the wicked, protects the saintly.

16Seeing the dreadful [age of] Kali, full of compassion for the living beings,
He took birth in Navadvipa, bringing His associates and companions with Him.

17Sri Chaitanya-raya, to whom the destitute are dear as life,
on whom Brahma, Shiva and Purandara meditate —

18be merciful to me, son of Jagannatha:
I shall describe something of the Rasika-mangala.

19Then I worshipped Nityananda-Balarama,
whose incomparable beauty surpasses tens of millions of Kamadevas.

20The poor, the lowly — every single person, down to the chandalas —
by giving them bhakti for Krishna He delivered the three worlds.

21Bowing down, I worship Shachi and Jagannatha;
I worship Hadai Pandita and Padmavati.

22I worship Lakshmi and Vishnupriya, the two Thakuranis;
I worship Vasudha and Jahnava, the wives of the elder brother.14

23With devotion I worship Advaita Acharya,
by whose mercy bhakti for Chaitanya arises.

24With joy I have now worshipped Sita Thakurani,
bhakti itself in the descent of Sri Chaitanya.

25I worship Sri Achyutananda, the son of Advaita;
I worship all the household of Sita Thakurani.

26I worship Virabhadra-raya, radiant in body,15
whose manifestation is famed throughout the earth.

27Together with their households I worship all the companions,
so that Rasika's glory may shine forth in my heart.

28With joy I worshipped Ramai and Sundarananda,
whose greatness is manifest on earth.

29I worship Gauridasa Thakura — Subala-raya;
everyone sings of him as dear to Nityananda.

30The whole world calls him an intimate friend (priya-narma-sakha);
in his line the Vaishnava Shyamananda appeared.16

31If that Prabhu grants [me] his mercy,
then I shall spread the Rasika-mangala.

32With respect I worship Uddharana Datta;
I worship Premeshvara, a follower of Chaitanya.17

33With humble entreaty I worship Murari Thakura;
with devotion I worshipped Kamalakara.

34I worship the two, Purushottama and Manohara;
I worshipped the feet of Kaliya Krishnadasa.18

35I worshipped the eight Giris, most dear to Chaitanya;
I worshipped the eight Puris, the elders of all.

36I worshipped the eight Bharatis, great mahajanas,
who had Vishvambhara accept sannyasa.19

37I worship the eight boys, followers of Chaitanya;
I worship the sixty-four mahantas, all the companions.20

38With great joy I worship the guru's line;
I worship Balarama, Bada Thakura, Haridasa.21

39I worship Govinda Gosvami, Thakura Mahesha;
especially I worship Durlabha Thakurani.22

40I worship Hridayananda, who brought light to the line;23
I worshipped the feet of all [his] servants and all the household.

41Together with their associates and companions I worship [them], the abode of all virtues; I worship all the Vaishnavas, bowing down [to them].

42I worship all the brahmanas, the best of all sannyasis;
I worship the seven seas, the earth with all that moves and does not move.

43Among these I joyfully worshipped the holy places,
by hearing of which bhakti for Krishna becomes manifest.

44I worship Sri Vrindavana, Madana-gopala,
Sri Govinda, Gopinatha, Sri Banka-vihara.24

45I worship Radha-vallabha, the graceful Thakura;25
I worship Kalindi-Yamuna, all of Vraja-pura.

46I worship Gokula, Mathura, Sri Keshava-raya,
by hearing of whom all sins are destroyed.26

47I worship Yadava-raya, the lord of Gokula;
I worshipped Gopala-raya, the holder of Govardhana.

48Then I worshipped Dvaraka and Ranchhor-raya:27
that abode of Krishna is greater than Vaikuntha.

49I worship Badarikashrama and Nara-Narayana;
I worship the Gandaki, the Gomati, Naimisharanya.

50I worship Prabhasa, Pushkara, the tirtha of the Godavari;
I worship the Narmada, the Sarasvati, the Sindhu, the Kaveri.

51I worshipped Ayodhya and Kurukshetra, holy abodes;
I worship Setubandha and every place where Hari [resides].

52I worshipped Hastinapura, the home of the Pandavas,
where Sri Krishna stays for the sake of His devotees.

53I worship Kanchi and Avantika, most holy places:
age after age the seven cities are the abodes of Hari.28

54I worship Sri Purushottama, the lord of Nilachala,29
Gaya, the Ganga, Varanasi, Prayaga and the rest.

55I worship the Bhagirathi and Navadvipa, the great place,
the abode of Sri Chaitanyachandra Mahaprabhu.

56I worship Gangasagara, famed throughout the world;
I worship holy Navadvipa and Tamralipta.30

57I worshipped the three places — heaven, earth and the netherworld;
among them I worshipped all the holy abodes.

58Be merciful to me, all of you — I bow down [to you] —
so that I may expound the Rasika-mangala.

59Briefly I shall speak of two or four of the elders;
by Rasika's mercy I worship the feet of them all.

60I worship Gopiramana, the adhikari [of the service] of Chaitanya;
I worship Sri Rama Thakura, possessed of every virtue.31

61I worshipped the two, Krishnananda and Dvarika;
I worship Achyuta and Bhavani, dear to Krishna.32

62I worship Prasada Thakura and Balaramadasa,
who lived together with Shyamananda's younger brother.33

63Manohara, full of bhava, renounced, devoted to Krishna;
I worship the feet of Kishora the teacher.

64I worship Sri Tulasidasa, the guru of sankirtana,
who from his birth lived together with Rasika.34

65At the festival of sankirtana he receives the first worship:
Rasika honours him with cloth and ornaments.

66When Rasika cannot manage to water Tulasi,
he offers [the water] at the feet of Tulasi[dasa] and drinks it with a joyful heart.35

67I worship all the elders, holding their feet,
so that I may sing Rasika's praise at every moment.

68I worship the feet of all the Vaishnavas of Shyamananda;
[I name] ten or twenty of the chief ones — this is a brief account.

69Do not hold against me any fault of order:
in the course of the book I shall tell of everything.

70I worship Yadavendradasa, the elder [brother] of Nityananda;36
I worship Sri Kishora and Sri Balakadasa.

71Vaishnavadasa, Gopinathadasa, Manohara;
I worship Damodara-prabhu, the servant of Krishna.37

72His voice choked with prema, his eyes filled with tears,
in the bliss of Krishna he weeps constantly night and day.

73Damodara knows nothing but Krishna;
he made very many disciples who took the one sole shelter.

74His union with Rasika is undivided;
to such a Damodara, a jewel among men, I bow.

75With joy I worshipped the brahmana Govindadasa;
I worshipped Gopala, Balabhadra, Haridasa.38

76I worshipped Govinda, the mahajana of Vrindavana;
I worship the feet of Shyamasundara and Uddhava.

77I worship the two, Shyamadasa and Jagannatha;
I worship the feet of Kaviraja Balabhadra.

78With devotion I worship Chintamanidasa;
I worship Sri Radhavallabhadasa, pure of mind.

79Anantadasa, Raghunathadasa of Mathura;
I worship the brahmana Padmanabha and Gangadharadasa.

80I worship Sri Radhamohana, the brahmana Shirikara;39
with respect I worship merciful Kanudasa.

81With reverence I worshipped Govindadasa and Bhudhara;
I worship Radhacharana and Purushottama, the best of brahmanas.

82I worship Ananta, Radhavallabha, Radhadhara,
Gokula, Krishna-smarana, the brahmana Damodara.40

83I worship Sri Shyamaranginidasa, the best of sadhus;
I worship Sri Shyamatarangi, a brahmana, the best of sadhus.

84Abhaya, Ramagovinda — I worshipped them all;
Ananda, Mathurashyama, pure in body.

85I worship Madhuvanadasa, a companion of Krishna;
each one of them has hundreds and hundreds of disciples, very many.

86I worship Sri Anandananda, a worthy brahmana;
I worshipped the descendants of Divakara, kind of heart.41

87With great joy I worship Sri Mathuradasa of the gopas;
with joy I worshipped Mathuradasa of Gauda.42

88Jagannathadasa, Radhavallabha, Bhudhara,
Ramadasa, Sri Chaitanyadasa, the best of brahmanas —

89their feet I worship, rejoicing;
I worship Sri Krishnadasa and Gopaladasa.

90I worship Mukunda-bhupati, a servant of Shyamananda,
whose poetic gift is manifest in all four directions.43

91I worship Sri Keshava Shiromani, greatly steadfast;
I worship Sachuda Sri Jagannatha, full of sattva.44

92With joy I worshipped Bhrigu and Sri Purushottama;
I worshipped Bhudeva and Sri Chaitanyadasa.

93I worship the vaidya Sri Gopaladasa, the fortunate;
I worship the brahmanas Shyama, Rasika, Govinda.

94Madana-mohanadasa, the brahmana Gadadhara;
I worship the brahmana Balabhadra and Vamshi, the best of brahmanas.

95I worship the brahmana Purushottama, greatly fortunate,
for whom Prabhu Shyamananda is caste, wealth and life.

96I worship the brahmana Damodara, a servant of Shyamananda,
whose true abode is at Shyamananda's holy feet.

97With all his family he gave himself over to Shyamananda;
he knows nothing but guru, Krishna and the sadhus.

98I worship Sri Mathuradasa, a great mahajana:
all [his] wealth and people he surrendered to Shyamananda.

99A dear disciple of Shyamananda, prema-bhakti embodied —
for him Prabhu Shyamananda is family, character and caste.

100The brahmana Haridasa, Vanamali, the best of brahmanas,
Radhakrishna, Dharambara, the vaishya Narayana;

101I worshipped Gauranga, Purushottama, Madhava;
I worship the brahmana Gopala, Manohara, Bhudeva.

102I worship Govinda Bhattacharya, who lives in Vanga:
in Vanga he made [the glory of] Shyamananda manifest.45

103I worship Sri Kishoradasa and Kanudasa,
Sri Mathuradasa of the gopas, Rasamayadasa.46

104I worship Sri Gaurangadasa and Manoharadasa;
I worship all the Shyamanandis, wherever each one lives.

105I worship Nilambaradasa and Sri Ananta-raya;
then I worshipped the worthy Sanatana.

106With joy I worshipped Thakura Vishnudasa,
who constantly delights [in the company of] Rasika.

107Then I worshipped Shyamadasi Thakurani,
Rasika's wife, prema-bhakti embodied.47

108A disciple of Shyamananda, devoted to her husband, mother of the world;
from her birth her service to Govinda has been known to the world.

109Then I worship Sri Devaki, Rasika's daughter,
a disciple of Shyamananda: the eldest sister, she is [our] mother.

110I worship Radhananda Thakura, Rasika's son,
a dear disciple of Shyamananda, endowed with every virtue.48

111Absorbed in Krishna, his heart is enchanted by the rasa of prema;
the streams from his eyes drench his whole body.

112He is full of all the shastras, a great scholar,
skilled in music, known to the world.

113I worshipped Sri Krishna Bhanja-deva, the maharaja,
who with firm faith serves and worships Shyamananda's feet.49

114A dear disciple of Shyamananda, the moon that illumines his line,
in whose land is the bliss of great festivals of service to Krishna.

115A king wholly devoted [to Krishna], known to the world,
dedicated to Hari-nama, always practising [it].

116In his heart dwell the sixty-four limbs of bhakti;50
everyone proclaims him devoted to the brahmanas.

117Is it Parikshit, Ambarisha, Sanaka and his brothers
who took birth in the form of bhakti for Krishna? He has won renown.51

118By the strength of his piety the best of kings, mighty and formidable:
hostile kings come and become servants at his feet.

119Such a king, a devotee of Krishna — be merciful to me:
I shall sing Rasika's glory, sitting steadfast.

120With devotion I worship Krishnanandadasa,
who has no other refuge than Shyamananda.

121I worship the chaste Vrindavati, Rasika's daughter,
humble and patient, whom the world praises.

122With joy I worshipped Krishnagati, pure of mind,
Rasika's middle son, renowned in the world.

123Mad with prema for Krishna, he does not know day from night;
such is Krishnagati, whose life's treasure is Krishna.

124Rasika's youngest son is Radhakrishnadasa,
dear to Shyamananda; [Krishna] is manifest in his pure heart.52

125Rasika's son, filled with the bliss of prema,
kind to all living beings — I worship those feet.

126Prasada, Gopala, Govinda, Ramadasa,
Madhava, Kishora, Radhamohana — those servants;

127and I worshipped the feet of Purushottamadasa;
the gopa Ankura — both are servants of Sri Shyamananda.53

128Krishnadasa Dariya, Radhavallabhadasa —
the servants among the Shyamanandis cannot be counted.54

129I worship Jagannatha, the servant of Achyuta's son;55
I worship Ananta, Sridhara and Kashinatha.

130Then I worshipped Nilambara Shirikara,
Kapileshvara, Gangadasa — all the companions.

131I worship Sri Shyamagopala, a great mahajana;
I worshipped the two, Chintamani and Vihari.

132Dinashyama, Ramakrishna, Shyama, Manohara,
Gopinatha, Vaidyanatha — all the companions.

133The Shyamanandis are numberless — how many names shall I take?
One by one I bow down to them all.

134Be merciful to me, all of you, accept me:
I shall proclaim something of Rasika's glory.

135Rolling at his feet, I worship my father Rasamaya;
then I worshipped my mother, devoted to her husband.

136Husband and wife, both, and five sons —
all took shelter at Rasika's feet.56

137I worshipped my paternal uncle, Vamshi Mathuradasa,
who is renowned among the first Shyamanandis.57

138I worship with devotion all the elders,
pure of mind, in my mother's line and my father's line.

139In the line of the gopas we all were born;
Shyamananda's two feet are [our] family, character and caste.

140Gopijana-vallabha, Haricharanadasa,
Madhava, Rasikananda, Kishoradasa —

141the five brothers, sons of Sri Rasamaya,
whose caste, wealth and life is Achyuta's son.58

142Vallabha's son is the renowned Radhavallabha,
whose mother and father is Rasikendra, the crest-jewel [of devotees].59

143Together with their families they are Rasika's servants;
they constantly abide with Rasika.

144As once upon the Pandavas and other poor, suffering people
Krishna kept His watchful gaze without cease,60

145[so,] by the power of the feet of Rasika, the devotee of Krishna,
no sorrow touches [them] or their families.

146Apart from Rasikendra they know nothing of all this —
puja, meditation, austerity, japa, the eightfold sadhana.61

147With their whole being they serve Rasika;
regarding them as servants, he protects them all.

148As Krishna, the friend of the poor, is a shelter and a shield,
so still more is [His] devotee a shelter, [like] one's own brother.62

149Thus the whole [of our] family abides at Rasika's feet
constantly — be it night, be it day.

150Rasika's paternal uncle, Tulasi Thakura,
every year urgently commands [me]:63

151"Seeing the prema for Krishna throughout the land of Utkala,
describe Rasika's glory!"

152Prabhu is embarrassed on hearing his own virtues —
fearing that embarrassment, I did not make [it] known.64

153At that time Rasika-shekhara of Berhapal,
laughing playfully, answered everyone:65

154"There will be a Shyamanandi who is so fortunate —
[who it is,] all the Shyamanandis devoted to Krishna decide.66

155So that all people may sing of this whole community,
it is good if someone describes [it] thus."

156Having received that encouragement, I took the command upon my head,
quickly honouring Rasika's feet, [placing them] upon my head.

157Remembering the lotus feet of Sri Krishna,
I shall describe something of Rasika's glory.

158Gopijana-vallabha, a servant of Sri Shyamananda,
has dared to make something known.

159The glory of a devotee is a boundless, fathomless ocean:
Brahma, Shiva, Indra and the others cannot find its limit.

160The greatness of a devotee is many times greater than Krishna['s]: [Krishna] constantly goes about [after His devotees] in hope of the dust of their feet.67

161Such is Rasika-Murari, most dear to Krishna:
even with ten million mouths I could not tell his virtues.

162I am utterly poor and lowly, wretched, in a sorry plight;
whatever is spoken — it is Rasika, the lord of [my] life, who speaks it.

163Who can tell of the boundless ocean of [his] pastimes?
Whatever appears to me by Shyamananda's mercy,

164I, relying on his command, shall make known —
something of Rasika-deva's holy glory.

165Without intelligence, without learning, I am of wicked mind;
what could I know of Rasika-deva's holy glory?

166All the Shyamanandis devoted to Krishna commanded me
to proclaim Rasika-deva's glory.

167Being a tiny person, I am very bold:
show favour, all of you, that [my] heart's wish may be fulfilled.

168I shall describe something — a description of [his] nature —
as the son of Achyuta, like a magician, makes [me] dance.68

169Do not mind any faults in the order [of the narrative];
may sadhus and learned people listen with affection.

170I shall tell something — the Rasika-mangala;
in the three worlds fortunate people will hear [it].

171Devotees of Sri Krishna, each abiding in his own place,
hear the Sri Rasika-mangala day and night.

172To hear it is a joy to the ears, to sing it is full of rasa;
merely by hearing it, one easily crosses [the ocean of] worldly existence.

173To destroy the terrible darkness of Kali, the impenetrable gloom,
[he] appeared in the form of a devotee.69

174As by hearing Krishna's qualities one crosses [the ocean of] worldly existence,
so merely by hearing a devotee's qualities one overcomes the three times.

175Whoever even once hears this with his ears,
in that very moment millions upon millions of great sins are destroyed.

176Release from all bonds and prema-bhakti come [to one]
who hears the holy praise — the Rasika-mangala.

177To the poor [it gives] wealth, to the childless a son;
hearing the Rasika-mangala takes away grief and sorrow.

178Supreme, exclusive bhakti arises at once [in one]
who reads [it] with love.

179All living beings suffer from the bite of Time —
recite, all of you, the mantra — the Rasika-mangala!

180Whoever reads or hears [it] is not devoured by the wheel of Time;
at once the noose of the bondage of worldly existence is destroyed.

181Effortlessly [he gains] wife, sons and every strength,
wealth, people, prema-bhakti, the highest good.

182Let no one disregard [it], saying, "It is composed in the common tongue" —
a venomous snake never at any time gives up its poison.70

183Listen attentively, all of you, leaving other talk;
having heard, destroy the pain of the bondage of worldly existence.

184Especially for the Shyamanandi Vaishnavas [this] is life:
Rasikendra-chudamani is their caste, life and wealth.

185Those who hear his qualities with faith
attain Rasika's feet without delay.

186In Patala the Nagas hear [it];
in heaven the devas hear, on earth the sadhus.71

187Sing with your own mouths the qualities of Krishna's devotee:
the four Vedas sing that Bhagavan is subject to His devotees.72

188O you most wise, all of you, do not impute any faults [to me];
setting aside [thought of] all faults, listen with joy.73

189Women, men and others, be they children or old people —
whoever hears [it] with whatever desire,

190merely by hearing, the desire is completely fulfilled:
wealth, grain, sons, grandsons, fame, a home full of prosperity.

191Release from all bonds [and] prema-bhakti come
merely by hearing the praise of Rasika.

192The Purva-vibhaga is supremely full of rasa:
having heard it, all living beings, cross over [the age of] Kali.

193Hear the Rasika-mangala, all friends:
without delay you will obtain the treasure of prema-bhakti for Krishna.

194Adorning himself with Shyamananda's feet,
the son of Rasamaya joyfully composed [this].

Thus in the Purva-vibhaga of the Sri Rasika-mangala ends the first lahari, called "Obeisances to the Vaishnavas".

Notes

  1. The mangala-shlokas at the beginning of the lahari are numbered separately in the edition (॥ 1 ॥–॥ 7 ॥), and from the song (after the raga and the ghosha, at the word "গীত") the numbering starts again from 1 and runs to the end of the lahari. To keep the numbers distinct, the shlokas are labelled S1–S7; the numbers 1, 2… are the edition's.
  2. According to tradition, Krishna Himself wrote a line into Jayadeva's Gita-govinda (in the 10th canto) when the poet hesitated to write it. The "mark in the form of a dot" (bindu) is apparently the tilaka mark on Shyamananda's forehead: tradition says Sri Radha Herself placed it, and the distinctive tilaka of his followers is connected with this (cf. BR 15 on Radha's anklet). The line can also be read differently — "only Sri Shyamananda, [being] Srimati Radhika Herself, joyfully made [it]" — the author's exaltation of Shyamananda. According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, Shyamananda is a devotee and servant of Radha, a disciple of Hridaya Chaitanya, not Radhika Herself.
  3. So in the 1941 edition: "জয়মকৃতমুদা" (jayam akṛta mudā); the 1997 edition reads "স্বয়ম কৃতমুদা" (svayam akṛta mudā, "Herself joyfully made"), which fits the sense; translated by the latter reading.
  4. "A treasury of tenderness" — drava-nidhiḥ (literally "a treasury of melting", i.e. of a heart melting with compassion); the reading is confirmed by the 1941 edition, the sense is conjectural.
  5. The pair of Bhattas are Raghunatha Bhatta and Gopala Bhatta; together with Sanatana, Rupa, Raghunatha Dasa and Jiva they are the six Gosvamis of Vrindavana.
  6. Rasikendra ("the king of rasikas") is Rasikananda.
  7. The shloka has a double meaning: Murari is a name of Krishna ("the enemy of Mura") and also Rasika-Murari, i.e. Rasikananda. Bharati is Sarasvati, the goddess of speech. A chintamani is a wish-fulfilling gem.
  8. Raga Karuna-shri. The ghosha is the refrain repeated when the song is sung; the following laharis begin in the same way.
  9. Shyamananda was born at Dharenda (Utkala) in a family of gopas (sadgopas, an agricultural caste); hence "the moon of the cowherd clan".
  10. "Having descended" — avatīrṇa: the author speaks of Shyamananda as descending age after age. This is the author's exalted praise; according to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching it is the Lord who descends age after age (cf. 15), while Shyamananda is His eternal associate and servant.
  11. Durika is Shyamananda's mother.
  12. The three Thakuranis are Shyamananda's three wives.
  13. Hridayananda is Hridaya Chaitanya of Ambika (Kalna), Shyamananda's guru.
  14. Lakshmi (Lakshmipriya) and Vishnupriya are the wives of Sri Chaitanya; Vasudha and Jahnava are the wives of Nityananda, the Lord's "elder brother".
  15. Virabhadra (Virachandra; so in the 1997 edition) is Nityananda's son.
  16. In Krishna's pastimes Gauridasa Pandita is the cowherd boy Subala, Krishna's intimate friend (priya-narma-sakha). "Line" here means spiritual succession: Gauridasa is the guru of Hridaya Chaitanya, and he of Shyamananda.
  17. So in the edition (premeśvara). Possibly Parameshvara (Dasa), an associate of Nityananda, is meant; not identified.
  18. Many of those named in 28–39 — Sundarananda, Gauridasa, Uddharana Datta, Kamalakara (Pippalai), Purushottama, Kala (Kaliya) Krishnadasa, Mahesha (Pandita) — are traditionally counted among the twelve gopalas, the associates of Nityananda. Murari Thakura and Manohara are not identified here.
  19. Giri, Puri and Bharati are branches of the sannyasa order. Sri Chaitanya (Vishvambhara) received sannyasa from Keshava Bharati (CC, Adi 17; CB, Madhya 28).
  20. The "eight boys" are not identified. The sixty-four mahantas are the traditional list of Sri Chaitanya's associates.
  21. The line is unclear: "বলরাম বড় ঠাকুর বন্দো হরিদাসে" (balarāma baṛa ṭhākura bando haridāse) — it may also be understood as "Balarama [and] the elder Thakura Haridasa". The persons are not identified.
  22. Thakura Mahesha is apparently Mahesha Pandita, an associate of Nityananda. Govinda Gosvami and Durlabha Thakurani are not identified.
  23. So in the 1941 edition: "হৃদয়ানন্দন" (hṛdayānandana, possibly "son of Hridaya"); the 1997 edition reads "হৃদয়ানন্দ". Understood as Hridayananda, i.e. Hridaya Chaitanya (cf. 12), who "brought light" to Gauridasa's line.
  24. Madana-gopala, Govinda and Gopinatha are the Deities of Vrindavana served by the Gosvamis. Banka-vihara (baṅka-behāra, "the curved sporting One") is apparently the Deity Banke-bihari in Vrindavana.
  25. Radha-vallabha is a Deity in Vrindavana. "Graceful" — cikaniyā ("smooth, graceful, charming").
  26. Keshava-raya (Keshavadeva) is the Deity of Krishna in Mathura. Gopala-raya, "the holder of Govardhana", is apparently the Gopala found by Madhavendra Puri on Govardhana Hill (CC, Madhya 4). Yadava-raya, "the lord of Gokula", is not identified.
  27. Ranchhor-raya ("he who left the battlefield") is Krishna as the Deity of Dvaraka (also worshipped at Dakor, Gujarat).
  28. The seven cities (sapta-puri) are traditionally Ayodhya, Mathura, Maya (Haridvar), Kashi, Kanchi, Avanti (Avantika) and Dvaraka.
  29. Purushottama is Puri; its lord is Jagannatha.
  30. Tamralipta is the old name of Tamluk in southern Bengal, near the border of Utkala.
  31. Adhikari — "owner; one entrusted with the service". Gopiramana and Rama Thakura are not identified.
  32. Krishnananda and Dvarika are apparently Shyamananda's parents: according to tradition his father was named Krishna (Mandala) and his mother Durika (cf. 10); the edition's variant reading here is "দুরিকা" (durikā). Achyuta and Bhavani are Rasikananda's parents (cf. BR 15).
  33. "Who lived together with Shyamananda's younger brother" — śyāmānandānuja saṅge yā̃dera nivāsa; the line can be understood otherwise, and its sense is not quite clear. Prasada Thakura and Balaramadasa are not identified.
  34. Tulasidasa is possibly the same as Tulasi Thakura, Rasikananda's paternal uncle (150).
  35. A play on words: Tulasi is the sacred plant and also Tulasidasa's name. When he cannot water Tulasi, Rasika bathes Tulasidasa's feet with the water and drinks it.
  36. Literally "the elder of Nityananda" (nityānanda-jyeṣṭha): which Nityananda is meant (apparently one of the Shyamanandis, not the Lord) and in what sense "elder" is unclear. The edition's variant reading: "জ্যেষ্ঠ নেত্রানন্দ" — "the elder, Netrananda".
  37. Damodara is apparently the former yogi whom Shyamananda made his disciple (BR 15, 55–58).
  38. From here on (75–132) the author lists disciples of Shyamananda and Rasikananda; most of them are not identified. BR 15 (63–65) names among Shyamananda's disciples Radhananda, Purushottama, Manohara, Chintamani, Balabhadra, Jagadishvara, Uddhava, Akrura, Madhuvana, Govinda, Jagannatha, Gadadhara, Anandananda, Radhamohana. Where a word may be either a name or an epithet (e.g. Bhudhara, Bhudeva, Ananda), it is rendered as a name.
  39. Shirikara (শিরীকর, śirīkara; also 130) is apparently a surname, possibly an Odia form of shrikarana (the scribal caste). Taken as a surname.
  40. "Krishna-smarana" (kṛṣṇa-smaraṇa, "remembrance of Krishna") is taken as a name; it may be an epithet of Gokula: "Gokula, who remembers Krishna".
  41. Divakara is not identified.
  42. "Of the gopas" — gopa: of the gopa caste (like Shyamananda, see 5); "of Gauda" — gauṛīyā, a Bengali.
  43. Bhupati — "king, lord of the earth"; possibly part of the name. The person is not identified.
  44. So in the 1941 edition: "সচূড়" (sacūṛa, "with a topknot, with a crest") and "সত্ত্বশীল" (sattva-śīla); the first word is taken as a byname. Keshava Shiromani and Jagannatha are not identified.
  45. Vanga — eastern Bengal.
  46. Rasamayadasa is apparently Rasamaya, the author's father (cf. 135, 141).
  47. Shyamadasi is Rasikananda's wife; in BR 15 (30) she is called Ichchha. Shyamadasi is apparently her initiated name, received from Shyamananda (cf. 108).
  48. Radhananda is Rasikananda's eldest son (cf. 122, the middle son, and 124, the youngest); a Radhananda is also named in BR 15 (63) among Shyamananda's disciples.
  49. Krishna Bhanja is apparently a raja of Mayurbhanj (northern Utkala) of the Bhanja dynasty; the person is not identified. Vaidyanatha (132) is possibly Vaidyanatha Bhanja, according to tradition a disciple of Rasikananda; not established.
  50. The sixty-four limbs (angas) of bhakti are listed in Rupa Gosvami's Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu (1.2) and in CC, Madhya 22.
  51. Parikshit, Ambarisha, and the four Kumaras (Sanaka and his brothers) are great devotees of the Srimad-Bhagavatam. In the second line the 1997 edition reads "কৃষ্ণ ভক্ত রূপে" ("in the form of a devotee of Krishna").
  52. "[Krishna] is manifest in his pure heart" — śuddha hṛdaye prakāśa; the subject is not named; possibly "[bhakti] is manifest…" or "he is renowned [as] pure of heart".
  53. So in the 1941 edition: "গোপ অঙ্কুর দোঁহে" (gopa aṅkura dõhe, "the gopa Ankura — both"); the 1997 edition has "দেহে". Understood thus: Purushottamadasa and Ankura of the gopa caste — both servants of Shyamananda.
  54. Dariya (দাড়িয়া, dāṛiyā) is possibly a byname ("the bearded one") or a village name; not identified.
  55. Achyuta's son is Rasikananda (cf. 141). The line can also be read as "I worship Achyuta's son [and] the servant Jagannatha".
  56. Rasamaya is the author's father, a disciple of Rasikananda; the author does not name his mother. The five sons are listed in 140.
  57. The first word of the second line reads in the 1941 edition approximately as "আদ্য" (ādya, "first, original"), possibly "আত্ম"; the 1997 edition has "অন্য" ("other"): "renowned among the other Shyamanandis". Translated by the reading ādya; the reading is unclear. It is also unclear whether this is one person (Vamshi Mathuradasa) or two (Vamshi and Mathuradasa).
  58. Gopijana-vallabha is the author himself. Rasikananda here is one of his brothers, not the hero of the poem. "Kishoradasa" — kiśorera dāsa, literally "the servant of Kishora", taken as a name. Achyuta's son is Rasikananda (cf. 129).
  59. Vallabha is apparently the author himself (Gopijana-vallabha), and Radhavallabha his son. "Crest-jewel" — cūṛāmaṇi: "Rasikendra-chudamani" is an epithet of Rasikananda.
  60. Cf. Kunti's prayers on how Krishna protected the Pandavas in their calamities (SB 1.8).
  61. "They" are the author's family (cf. 140–145). Ashtanga-sadhana is eightfold yoga.
  62. "A shelter and a shield" — śaraṇa pañjara (pañjara, "cage, enclosure"), i.e. secure protection. "One's own brother" — sodara, literally "born of the same womb".
  63. Tulasi Thakura is apparently the same Tulasidasa, the "guru of sankirtana", whom Rasika honoured from birth (64–66; cf. note 34).
  64. Prabhu is apparently Rasikananda.
  65. Berhapal (বেঢ়াপাল, beṛhāpāla) is unidentified. Rasika-shekhara ("crest-jewel of rasikas") is taken as the name of a resident of Berhapal; the author also calls Rasikananda himself by this name (lahari 2, 4). The second line can also be understood as "…and all laughingly answered".
  66. So in the 1941 edition: "কাষ্ণ´" (the superscript mark is a displaced reph), taken as kārṣṇa ("devotees of Krishna"); likewise in 166. The 1997 edition reads "কাঞ্চ'", and in a quotation in that edition's preface "কার্য" ("affairs").
  67. Cf. SB 11.14.16: the Lord follows His desireless devotee in order to be purified by the dust of his feet. Thus the Lord Himself exalts His devotees.
  68. So in the 1941 edition: "স্বভাব বর্ণনা" (svabhāva varṇanā); the 1997 edition reads "স্বভাষ" ("in one's own language") or "ভাব". "Like a magician" — kuhake (kuhaka, a conjurer, magician). The son of Achyuta is Rasikananda.
  69. The subject is not named: apparently Rasikananda, whom the author speaks of as appearing "in the form of a devotee" (cf. note 10); it can also be understood of Sri Chaitanya — the Lord who came in the form of a devotee. According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching Rasikananda is a devotee and associate, not an incarnation of the Lord.
  70. "Composed in the common tongue" — bhāṣā-bandha: in Bengali, not in Sanskrit. The point of the comparison: the power [of the narrative] does not depend on its language, just as a snake is venomous at all times.
  71. "On earth" — in the 1941 edition mañce (মঞ্চে), taken as martye ("in the world of men"); the 1997 edition reads "মর্তে".
  72. So in the 1941 edition: "গাও" (gāo, "sing"); it can also be understood as "[Krishna] with His own mouth sings the qualities of His devotee".
  73. The 1941 edition reads "না হইবে" ("there will not be"); the 1997 edition reads "না লইবে" ("do not impute"); translated by the latter reading.
